newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - ASM Lithography jumps.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - ASM Lithography jumps.

text.p: ASM Lithography, a Dutch semiconductor equipment maker, stood out among companies with American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) after winning a big order, traders said on Thursday.
ASM Lithography rose to a fresh 52-week high of 70-1/8 in early trading before settling back to 69-5/8 near midday, or 6-7/8 higher the previous day's close.
"It was up there," said one dealer. "No other (European) ADR came close to it."
Earlier ASM said it won an order worth more than $150 million from Micron Technology Inc to install systems at the memory chipmaker's facilities in Boise, Idaho.
Elsewhere, European oil companies appeared to be recovering somewhat after recent analyst forecasts that saw oil prices dropping in the near future.
"They're in line or slightly higher with where they closed in Europe today," the dealer said.
Royal Dutch Petroleum Co was up 13/16 at 54-3/8, and British Petroleum Co Plc was 3/16 higher at 78-13/16.
Meanwhile, Latin American ADRs were trading slightly lower amid some mild profit-taking.
"We've had a tremendous run in the last eight or nine days and we're now seeing some profit-taking," another trader said.
Argentine energy company YPF SA was 3/16 lower at 31-7/16, while Brazil's Telebras SA was down 1-5/16 at 163-9/16.
But Telefonica de Argentina SA was 5/16 stronger at 37-7/8 and Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) was up 5/16 at 53-5/8.
Overall, the 814-strong ADR group was up 0.18 percent in early afternoon trading.
ADRs allow U.S. trade of foreign shares.
